messages.message:
Patch Set 2:

(3 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Some concerns. The design objection from the patchset 1 thread is still open on this revision: ordering a bucket purely by logical offset, with no object identity and no bounded per-object batch, was questioned as counter-productive for backend block allocation and as a way to starve an already-queued request. Patchset 2 answers it by documenting the limitation in the commit message and the man page, but the comparison itself is unchanged, so the request for bucket/object selection followed by a size-bounded offset-ordered batch has not been answered in code and the thread is unresolved. Since the key is opt-in and off by default, nothing here demands an immediate re-spin, but that thread looks like it should close before this lands. The inline items are optional nits to pick up on the next refresh.

parents.subject: LU-17296 tests: one-tenant mClock baseline against FIFO

commit.subject: LU-17296 nrs: order BRW RPCs by offset inside an mClock class
commit.message:
LU-17296 nrs: order BRW RPCs by offset inside an mClock class

Inside one mClock class bucket the queue is FIFO. A fair shared HDD
OST loses the seek order that the ORR policy gives.

Add a locality= key to the mClock start command. The key puts the
read RPCs and the write RPCs of one bucket in a red-black tree. The
logical offset of the first fragment orders the tree. Requests with
an equal offset keep the arrival order. The FIFO list still holds
every request, so the emptiness of the list keeps its meaning for
the class bucket. The selection between the buckets does not change.

A class key names a job, a user, a NID or a project, never an object.
One class bucket can therefore hold the requests of many objects.
The tree compares the offsets of all of them. The key targets the
case of one large object for each class. A key of (object FID,
offset) needs the batch mechanism of the ORR policy. The locality
key does not add that mechanism.

The TBF policy does not hold the key, and a TBF start with the key
returns -EINVAL.

The YAML rule dump gains an offset_insert counter. The counter counts
the requests that the enqueue path puts in the offset tree. Test
test_77xe runs the load with locality=1 and then with locality=0. The
sum must be above 0 with the key, and exactly 0 without it.

The mClock request grows to 64 bytes, and the request union of the
NRS layer grows with it. A build assertion records the new bound.

Test-Parameters: trivial testlist=sanityn env=ONLY="77xe",ONLY_REPEAT=3
Signed-off-by: Chris Horn <chorn@ddn.com>
